stem: Shreekar bought a Laptop with \(10\%\) discount on printed price. The printed price of that Laptop was \(\text{₹}\,50{,}000\). \(18\%\) GST was charged on discounted price. Complete the activity to find the amount of CGST and SGST. What amount did Shreekar pay?
One of the roots of the quadratic equation \(5m^2 + 2m + k = 0\) is \(\dfrac{-7}{5}\). Complete the activity to find the value of \(k\).
solution: Since \(\dfrac{-7}{5}\) is a root, put \(m = \dfrac{-7}{5}\) in the equation: \(5\left(\dfrac{-7}{5}\right)^2 + 2\left(\dfrac{-7}{5}\right) + k = 0\). So \(5\times \dfrac{49}{25} - \dfrac{14}{5} + k = 0\), i.e. \(\dfrac{49}{5} - \dfrac{14}{5} + k = 0\), giving \(\dfrac{35}{5} + k = 0\), so \(7 + k = 0\) and \(k = -7\).

stem: Two numbers differ by 3. The sum of twice the smaller number and thrice the greater number is 19. Find the numbers.
solution: Let the greater number be \(x\) and the smaller be \(y\). Then \(x - y = 3\) and \(2y + 3x = 19\). From the first, \(x = y + 3\). Substitute: \(2y + 3(y + 3) = 19\), so \(5y + 9 = 19\), giving \(5y = 10\) and \(y = 2\). Then \(x = 5\). The numbers are 5 and 2.

stem: Sachin invested some amount in a National Saving Certificate Scheme. In the first year he invested \(\text{₹}\,5{,}000\), in the second year \(\text{₹}\,7{,}000\), in the third year \(\text{₹}\,9{,}000\) and so on. Find the total amount that he invested in 12 years.
solution: The yearly investments \(5000, 7000, 9000, \ldots\) form an A.P. with \(a = 5000,\ d = 2000,\ n = 12\). \(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}\left[2a + (n-1)d\right] = \dfrac{12}{2}\left[2\times 5000 + 11\times 2000\right] = 6\left[10000 + 22000\right] = 6\times 32000 = \text{₹}\,1{,}92{,}000\).

stem: There are six cards in a box, each bearing a number from 0 to 5. Find the probability of each of the following events, that: (1) The number on the card drawn is a natural number. (2) The number on the card drawn is a whole number.

Draw a histogram of the following data:

| Height of Students (cm) | No. of Students |
|---|---|
| 135–140 | 4 |
| 140–145 | 12 |
| 145–150 | 16 |
| 150–155 | 8 |
solution: Take the class-intervals of height (cm) on the X-axis and the number of students on the Y-axis (a continuous scale, since the classes are continuous). Draw adjacent rectangles (bars with no gaps) on each class-interval with heights equal to the frequencies: \(135\text{–}140\to 4\), \(140\text{–}145\to 12\), \(145\text{–}150\to 16\), \(150\text{–}155\to 8\). The resulting adjacent bars form the required histogram.
